question: Which lossless runtime levers reduce the wall-clock cost of chain-of-thought for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (experts in system RAM) on Slink?
hardware: Ryzen 9 3900X (12C/24T), 62 GiB DDR4, RTX 2070 SUPER 8 GiB; GLM-4.7-Flash forge teacher resident on the GPU (2.5 GiB) as an allowed neighbour

params.followup: In one sentence, what is the single most important line to change?

prompts: 12 fixed dev-split secpatch prompts (6 root_cause, 6 remediate; first by file order); never held-out items

arms.lever: experts of the last 3 layers in VRAM (--n-cpu-moe 37)
fast Liquid model (8B total, 1B active), experts in RAM beside GLM
larger Liquid model (24B total, 2B active), experts in RAM

primary_metric: generated tokens per wall-clock second over all 12 prompts (includes prefill and verification overhead)
losslessness: every output's sha256 (reasoning + answer text) compared with A0 at temperature 0
decision_rule: An arm is adopted only if tokens_per_wall_s >= 1.10 x A0 AND at least 11/12 outputs are identical to A0. Divergent outputs are inspected and reported, never dropped.

predictions.A1: +3% to +8% (3 of 40 expert layers moved; decode is bounded by system-RAM expert reads)
predictions.A2: +5% to +30% (reasoning about code repeats identifiers and quoted lines)
predictions.A3: +20% to +60% (vendor claims 1.5-2x on full-GPU setups; verification of 2-3 tokens can route to different experts in RAM, so less amortization here)
predictions.A6: 3x-8x less wall time; quality drop on root-cause CWE likely
predictions.A7: 5x-15x less wall time than A0; quality below A0
predictions.A8: 3x-8x less wall time than A0; quality near the 4B

combination: After the preregistered arms, the best adopted levers may be combined as an exploratory arm A5, reported as exploratory.
not_tested_here: hot-expert caching (per-expert VRAM placement): stock llama.cpp stores a layer's 256 experts in one tensor; needs routing-skew measurement and an engine change first
reasoning-token reduction (budgets, early exit): changes outputs, so it is measured on secpatch quality, not here
amendment: Before any run, after the owner set the bar at 5-10x real-world speed: added quality grading (secpatch graders), turn-2 follow-up latency with prompt caching, and arms for the large factors: 35B reasoning off (A6), and the fast Liquid models LFM2.5-8B-A1B (A7) and LFM2.5-24B-A2B (A8). A6-A8 change outputs, so they are judged on time per correct answer, not identity.
primary_metric_realworld: wall seconds per correct answer over the 12 prompts, turn-1 plus turn-2; real-world multiplier = A0 seconds-per-correct / arm seconds-per-correct. Target for the best stack: >= 5x.
quality_floor: An output-changing arm counts only if its correct answers >= A0 correct - 1 (12 prompts: a screen, low power; winners are confirmed on the full dev set before adoption).
